You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**. Static assets in public/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-03-assets.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED.

EFFICIENCY: use find/du/file and ImageMagick `identify` in batched shell calls to inventory quickly. Only open (Read) an image when its filename does not make its content obvious, and prefer opening a downscaled copy written to /tmp. Do not open more than ~20 images.

YOUR AUDIT: VISUAL ASSET INVENTORY with a KEEP / REWORK / REPLACE / REMOVE verdict per asset. The owner's rule: the default for DECORATIVE assets is REPLACE; nothing gets recycled merely because it exists; the logo/wordmark and legitimately-sourced game artwork are the main KEEP candidates; screenshots are never an asset source.
Produce:
1. public/** inventory: every image/svg/video/font/ico file. Group by folder (logos, game art/heroes/posters, illustrations, backgrounds, icons, og images, favicons, one-click app icons, OS icons, region/flag images, misc). For each (or each GROUP where a folder holds many near-identical files): path, dimensions, size, format, what it depicts, where referenced (grep the filename; flag UNREFERENCED files), and a verdict with a one-line reason. For game artwork note whether it appears to be official key art vs generated, and any licensing notes findable in the repo.
2. Logo / wordmark treatments: every Nxeon logo variant (svg/png, colour variants, favicon, og image, email logo, loading logo), where used, inconsistencies.
3. Inline decorative graphics inside portal components: grep for `<svg` in components/customer, components/portal, app/dashboard — glows, blobs, orbs, grids, mesh gradients, noise, hero backdrops, gradient text. List each with file:line and verdict. Distinguish DECORATIVE svg from FUNCTIONAL svg (icons, charts) — charts and icons are not decoration.
4. CSS-generated decoration: background-image utilities, radial/conic gradients in globals.css or components, animated backgrounds, blur orbs — list with verdict.
5. Empty-state / onboarding / success / error illustrations: what exists, style consistency, verdict.
6. Game catalogue visuals: the manifest/lib file listing games, image fields, aspect ratios, per-game hero/poster/logo, count of games, missing images, mixed aspect ratios.
7. One-click app / OS / region imagery: what represents Ubuntu/Debian/Docker/WordPress etc. and regions, source and verdict.
8. Email template imagery (lib/email-templates.ts or an emails/ dir) — list only, verdict.
9. Summary table: counts per verdict, plus the shortlist of what a NEW asset library must provide (categories + rough counts), without designing them.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary with counts per verdict.
